analysis:
Both changed files are test-only. FlintResponseFormatTests.swift line 362 (head) changes `case .info: break` to `case .info, .logprobs: break`. QwenJSONAnswerServingTests.swift line 107 adds `.logprobs` to the ignored cases in an event switch. Both edits only keep the test event-handling switches exhaustive after a new `.logprobs` event case was added to the generation event enum. That enum change is in production code outside this batch. No production source, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, or coordinator/provider protocol code is touched, so TB-002, TB-009 and the other threat-model boundaries are unaffected by these diffs. The Flint tests still assert fail-closed behavior: errors never quote generated content, and tool-call frames are rejected when a response_format is present.

Open integration question: the production `.logprobs` event and where it is emitted. This includes whether logprobs of decrypted prompt or completion tokens could reach the response path or logs unencrypted (A-001, T-008). That code is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot conclude whether it is safe. The test diffs themselves introduce no regression.
